items.title: Extreme fatigue illness linked with changes to immune cells: study
items.description: Ella Engel saw many specialists before she was diagnosed with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome. Her blood may help researchers understand the condition.

items.title: Kremlin tells Australian embassy in Kyiv to evacuate amid parade tensions
items.description: The Australian embassy in Ukraine is on high alert after the Kremlin warned staff to evacuate ahead of possible "massive missile strikes" this weekend, as Moscow prepares to hold a scaled-down military parade.

items.title: Military parades and promises of peace ring hollower than ever
items.description: Displays of military strength and perpetual promises of peace do little to mask the reality that major powers aren't always able to control the wars they helped create.

items.title: Concerns for welfare of Victorian man last seen near Bibbulmun track
items.description: Samuel Whitsed, 27, was last seen on February 18 after he was dropped off near the popular hiking trail in Perth's south-eastern fringe, and police continue searching for him.

items.title: CSIRO to persist with job cuts despite $387 million funding injection
items.description: Australia's national science agency CSIRO will persist with job cuts to up to 350 roles despite an extra $387.4 million in funding announced from the federal government.

items.title: The social cost of having turned homes 'among the gum trees' into investments
items.description: Australia's regional housing crisis is decades in the making, the head of a research institute says. So can the federal budget fix it?

items.title: Live: Kangaroos take on Swans in Saturday opener ahead of Cats-Pies clash
items.description: The Sydney Swans travel to Docklands to face North Melbourne in the first of four AFL games on Saturday, before tonight's big clash between Geelong and Collingwood at the MCG. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Maroons suffer Origin blow with halfback Dearden needing ankle surgery
items.description: Queensland has lost its halfback for the State of Origin opener, with Tom Dearden needing ankle surgery. Follow live.

items.title: US importing more beef as demand soars and prices rise
items.description: The United States is importing more beef from Australia as its own supplies dwindle and demand soars.

items.title: One Nation's Farrer candidate unfazed by last-minute campaign criticisms
items.description: After three months of intense campaigning, voters in the NSW electorate say whoever wins today's poll must act on the promise to make noise in Canberra.

items.title: Massive ruby found in Myanmar, where gem mining has links to junta
items.description: Miners have unearthed a large ruby in Myanmar, which produces up to 90 per cent of the world's rubies.

items.title: Trump releases UFO files in 'unprecedented transparency'
items.description: The US government releases 160 previously classified files on alleged UFO sightings and alien life, including a photo of "unidentified phenomena" taken from the Moon's surface in 1969.

items.title: The warning from this city to other towns on the cusp of closing down coal
items.description: As Australia weans itself away from coal, aging power stations across the country have been reduced to smoke and rubble. But for communities at the coalface, there are serious and dramatic consequences.

items.title: Are we facing a global food crisis?
items.description: Experts are warning that high food prices and even food shortages are a serious risk if the US-Israeli war in Iran doesn't end soon. The United Nations says the window to prevent a full blown food crisis is closing rapidly. While the worst will initially be felt in Africa and South Asia, if the Strait of Hormuz doesn't open soon, it could turn into a global food crisis.

items.title: Four for the weekend: Lena Dunham, Kneecap and a fix-all stew
items.description: What we're watching, reading and cooking this weekend.

items.title: If you are not convinced by sardines, this is the dish to try
items.description: This simple and nutritious pasta dish is sure to satisfy those who already adore sardines, and it may just convert those who don't.

items.title: Iron Maiden's documentary is a victory lap celebrating 50 years
items.description: The Iron Maiden documentary is a 50-year history of heavy metal's flashiest band as told by their biggest fans.

items.title: Julie Bishop was adamant she wasn't going anywhere — until she did
items.description: December 31 was the date when Julie Bishop was due to finish her term as Australian National University chancellor, so why — after having repeatedly stated she would see her commitment through — did she leave months early?

items.title: Coalition's EV strategy risks appearing out of touch
items.description: The climate war is being won quietly, with nearly three in four One Nation voters eager to buy an EV.

items.title: 'Out of sight, out of mind' is the most dangerous response to 'ISIS brides'
items.description: The political energy spent on the "ISIS brides" has not been matched by serious attention to the deficiencies in Australia's counterterrorism architecture.

items.title: 'Powerful' symbol faces removal from the heart of Chinese community
items.description: The 26-year-old artwork is facing removal after the City of Sydney identified termite damage and cracking in the timber.

items.title: UK PM 'not going to walk away' despite catastrophic local election defeats
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer's Labour party has lost hundreds of seats in the local government election in England and has admitted defeat in Wales — which was previously Labour heartland.

items.title: The biofuel industry is ready to expand. Here's what it says is holding it back
items.description: Billions of dollars worth of investment will flow if the federal government mandates a percentage of biofuels be added to the nation's fuel supply, major investors say.

items.title: Attenborough at 100 'warm, well-informed and delightful company'
items.description: His legendary environmental documentaries have captivated generations, but away from the screen, Sir David Attenborough is "warm, well-informed and delightful company", too.

items.title: Depth of antisemitism exposed by anonymous witnesses before commission
items.description: Fear, concerns for safety and the impact on children dominated the first week of hearings of the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.
